subject: Live inference dropouts during peak - urgent

Subject: Live responses dropping during morning peak

Rafael,

We started seeing a pattern this morning around 07:50 PST where streaming responses from Redwood started truncating mid-response and some websocket connections timed out after ~35s. Impact: our checkout assistant returns partial answers and we see ~3% user-visible failures during the spike. We collected a short pcap and a sample request payloads (attached).

Timeline snippet:
- 07:49:10 - first partial response observed
- 07:52:02 - spike in websocket timeouts (client-side)
- 08:00:00 - rate peaked at ~420 rps to redwood-hosted endpoint

Can you triage? This is impacting checkout conversions. We need an ETA on mitigation. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Elena Park

Subject: Re: Live responses dropping during morning peak -- initial triage

Rafael / Grace — quick summary from the runtime side after looking at the logs Elena attached and our internal worker traces. Attaching server logs (server-logs-20261101.txt) and a short sample of the worker stack traces. Observations: 

- Around 07:49:45 UTC (07:49 PST), we see a burst that spikes sequence length (avg tokens per request jumped) and concurrent streaming sessions.
- Several inference worker processes reported transient OOM signals around the same window and restarted; when a worker restarts mid-request we currently close the upstream socket which results in a partial chunked response and a client-observed websocket close.
- Nginx front proxy has upstream_read_timeout set to 30s by default; combined with the sudden processing pause this surface causes the connection to be closed before the runtime recovers.
- There's evidence of KV cache thrashing (cache eviction pressure) which increases tail latency for long contexts and worsens the OOM hits.

Short-term mitigations we can push immediately (low risk):
1) Increase Nginx upstream_read_timeout to 60s for KartGo's route.
2) Enable automatic fallback policy for their route to a smaller quantized variant (reduces memory pressure).
3) Spin up an extra 2 dedicated workers in the pool and mark KartGo traffic to that pool via a routing override.

Medium-term: tune eviction policy for KV cache and add a restart guard so workers do not kill active requests (drain first). We'll open a ticket to prioritize.

I'll prepare a canary config change and a Grafana snapshot. ETA for the short-term push: 20-30 minutes after approval.

—Dev Patel
On-call Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: server-logs-20261101.txt

Subject: Re: Live responses dropping during morning peak — mitigation plan

Elena — thank you for the quick turnaround. Dev confirmed transient worker OOMs that cause upstream socket closures during spikes, which manifest as truncated streaming chunks and websocket timeouts on your side.

Proposed immediate actions (we will only proceed with your approval):
- Apply routing override to move KartGo to a dedicated pool (adds capacity + isolates memory pressure) — estimated 5 minute change with no downtime.
- Increase upstream_read_timeout to 60s for your route.
- Enable fallback to quantized model variant for requests exceeding X tokens (we can tune the threshold).

We can also schedule a 10-min maintenance window at 10:00 PST to apply the canary config and monitor. If you approve, we'll proceed and share Grafana live links and a post-mortem follow-up.

As a gesture for the regression you saw today, I'm opening an internal request for a one-time credit (pending leadership sign-off); I'll update you when approved.

Please confirm whether 10:00 PST works for the maintenance window and whether you approve the routing override.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
